title: Scaffolds & Tower Scaffolds
whatItIs: Scaffolds and tower scaffolds give a guarded working platform that prevents falls. Only trained, competent people may put them up, alter or take them down, and they must be inspected.

keyFacts.text: The top guard rail MUST be at least 950 mm high; gaps between rails MUST NOT exceed 470 mm.
A platform you could fall 2 m or more from MUST be inspected after assembly, after events affecting it and every 7 days.
Scaffolds MUST only be put up, altered or taken down by trained people, supervised by a competent person.
A scaffold not ready for use MUST carry warning signs and be physically blocked off.

keyFacts: Platforms should be fully boarded, with toe boards where objects could roll or be kicked off.
Moving a mobile tower: lower it to 4 m at most and check for power lines and potholes first.

b.label: Brick guards
points: Stop materials falling through gaps in the rails

onTheTest.question: A scaffold platform is 4 m high. How often must it be inspected while it stays in use?
options: Only when it is first put up
onTheTest.why: Work at Height Regs reg 12(4): a platform you could fall 2 m or more from must have been inspected in the previous 7 days.

onTheTest.question: A scaffold still being built has warning signs and a barrier at the access point. What should you do?
options: Use it if the lift you need looks finished
Keep off it until it's complete and inspected
Use it if you wear a harness
Move the barrier and check it yourself
onTheTest.why: Work at Height Regs Sch 3 para 11: a scaffold not available for use must carry warning signs and access must be physically blocked.

traps: Brick guards don't stop people falling: guard rails and toe boards are still needed.
Don't sheet a scaffold or fit debris netting without telling the supplier: it must be designed for it.
Don't climb a tower's end frames unless the rungs are designed for getting to the platform.
Never move a tower with people or materials on it, and never prop it on bricks or blocks.
